messages:
jia: Quick post: results from the rdl-7b quant bakeoff. ran FP8, AWQ, GPTQ (2-pass), and INT8 on the same eval set.

jia: TL;DR: AWQ with per-tensor works well for latency/cost but shows a ~1.8% avg LM-regression. GPTQ+per-layer rescue gets us within 0.4% but costs more CPU preproc. FP8 gives best quality but needs custom kernels.

alex: can you drop the numeric table?

jia: pasted minimal numbers below (perplexity delta vs fp32 / avg exact match delta):
```
scheme  | ppl_delta | em_delta
AWQ     | +2.1      | -1.8%
GPTQ    | +0.5      | -0.4%
INT8    | +3.4      | -2.6%
FP8     | +0.2      | -0.1%
```

maria: those AWQ numbers match what i saw on the customer prompt set. any idea where the 1.8% comes from (layers/heads)?

jia: digging into layer stats — we instrumented per-head activation moments during a 2k token pass. found a small subset of heads in layers 21-24 with extreme kurtosis and a few outlier channels that blow quant bins.

sam: hmm is this the same 'odd activation streak' pattern we saw on rdl-3b?

jia: similar shape but different layers. here's a quick snippet of the head score we used to flag outliers (z-score of abs(mean)/std over validation slices):
```
# compute head outlier score
for layer in range(L):
  for head in range(H):
    vals = activations[layer][head]
    score = abs(vals.mean()) / (vals.std() + 1e-6)
    if score > 8.0:
      flagged.append((layer, head, score))
```

maria: score>8 seems strict but reasonable. how many heads flagged?

jia: 12 heads across 4 contiguous layers (21-24). across heads they cover ~0.6% of params but their activations dominate a few tokens.

alex: previous approach was skip-quantize those layers entirely (layer-skip). did that help?

jia: we tried two mitigations in parallel: 1) layer-skip (fallback to fp32 for full layer), 2) headwise-clamp: per-head scale + clamp + small bias correction + optional skipping for top-k tokens.

jia: Results:
- layer-skip: removes most regression but increases tail latency by ~12% and memory by +6%
- headwise-clamp v1: reduces EM regression to ~0.6%, latency +2% (tiny), cost still ~AWQ baseline

sam: headwise-clamp sounds promising. what's the clamp formula?

jia: simple per-head per-row max/min computed from 99.9th percentile on calibration set, then a small rescale so global layer norms preserved. quick pseudo: 
```
scale = p99 / quant_max
tensor_clamped = clamp(tensor/scale, -quant_max, quant_max)
reproject = tensor_clamped * scale * correction_factor
```
correction_factor learned as linear fit on calibration outputs (~0.98-1.02).

maria: are we storing per-head scale metadata in the model artifact? that affects serving metadata size.

jia: yes small overhead: per-head float32 scale + correction ~ H*L*8 bytes — for 7b it's ~180KB. ok for hosted and dedicated.

alex: what about failure modes where clamped heads overflow on rare tokens?

jia: added a runtime fallback: if softmax divergence > 0.15 compared to cached fp32 prefix results, fall back to fp32 for that token window (cheap because rare). This eliminated the remaining 0.6% EM loss in canary.

ci-bot: build 2026.3.12.18 completed for rdl-7b-quant; artifacts: awq-head-clamp-v1, awq-head-clamp-v1-fallback.

sam: nice. any perf numbers for canary?

jia: canary (5% traffic on dedicated pool):
- awq baseline: p50=36ms p95=112ms cost=0.42x
- awq+head-clamp: p50=38ms p95=118ms cost=0.44x em_delta=-0.6%
- awq+head-clamp+fallback: p50=39ms p95=122ms cost=0.46x em_delta=-0.1%

maria: acceptable tradeoff if it fixes user-visible regressions. do we have A/B eval dashboards hooked up?

jia: yes linked to console evals. i've pushed the eval suite and prompt set. watch for any customer-facing regressions in the next 24h.

alex: action items?

maria: - run 24h canary and monitor EM/latency (link to eval)
maria: - run same head-clamp approach for rdl-13b calibration
sam: - add small unit test for softmax-divergence fallback
jia: - prepare rollout notes, include per-head metadata schema + storage impact

jia: ok will do. thanks all :thumbsup:

alex: one more ask: let's log which tokens triggered fallback (anonymized) for triage if the canary hits anything weird.

jia: added. logging includes token hash + timestamp + top-5 logits diff summary (no raw customer text).

maria: perfect.

sam: exciting — headwise rescue might be our default pattern for AWQ on hot models.

jia: agreed. will update the model onboarding checklist with a headwise outlier scan + clamp recipe.

jia: closing thread after canary completes, will reopen if any regressions.
